I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about dyeing with the woad (a dyeing plant), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed and he (peace be upon him) was dyed with the woad.'

key_terms.الْوَسْمَةِ: Woad (a plant used for blue dye)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to dye hair with woad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirmed the permissibility of dyeing with woad (al-wasmah), grounding this ruling in the noble precedent of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who was martyred while wearing it. This historical linkage not only validates the practice as a Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt but also elevates the dye to a symbol of dignity and continuity within the lineage of the Imams. The ruling underscores the practical application of prophetic traditions in daily life, emphasizing that such customs are embraced rather than discouraged.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Yunus, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the dyeing with the woad (a dyeing plant), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed and he<sup>asws</sup> dyed with the woad (a dyeing plant)’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from Yunus from abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about applying hair dye with woad. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. At the time al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was murdered he had applied hair dye with woad. 5 ”
